# TrackFlow company tools — MCP tool reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run mcp:tools -- --write docs/mcp/TOOLS.md` from the
     server's own tools/list. Do not edit by hand: a test compares them. -->

Server `trackflow-company-tools` 1.0.0. Transport: Streamable HTTP (stateless). Every request needs an OAuth bearer token (see `mcp-server.md`).

## Scopes

| Scope | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `incidents:read` | Read incidents: one by id or helpdesk reference, or a search. |
| `incidents:create` | Register new incidents. |
| `incidents:update` | Move an incident along its lifecycle (status changes). |
| `inventory:read` | Read products, stock and movement history. There is no write scope. |

There is no inventory write scope: the inventory is read-only on this server.

## Tool error codes

A refused or failed call is a tool result with `isError: true` whose text is JSON `{"error": "<code>", "message": "..."}`.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `insufficient_scope` | The access token is valid but lacks a scope this tool requires. `required_scopes` and `granted_scopes` say which. |
| `inventory_read_only` | A modification of inventory data was attempted. The inventory is read-only on this server: no scope and no tool can create products or record stock movements. |
| `invalid_arguments` | The arguments break the tool's input schema or rules; `problems` lists them. |
| `unknown_tool` | No tool with that name exists. Call tools/list. |
| `incident_not_found` | No incident has that id or helpdesk reference. |
| `product_not_found` | No product has that id. |
| `invalid_status_transition` | The incident lifecycle does not allow that status change; the message says which moves are available. |
| `upstream_rejected` | The Incidents Manager or the inventory refused the request; `field` and the message are theirs. |
| `upstream_unavailable` | The service behind the tool did not answer in time, could not be reached, or failed. Retrying later may work. |
| `upstream_auth_failed` | This server could not sign in to the inventory with its service account. |
| `internal_error` | The server failed unexpectedly; the details are in its log. |

## Tools

### `create_incident` — Create incident

- Required scopes: `incidents:create`
- Access: write on incidents
- Annotations: readOnlyHint=False, destructiveHint=False, idempotentHint=False, openWorldHint=False

Register a new incident in the Incidents Manager (`POST /api/incidents`). It starts in status `open`; the answer carries its new `id`.

Use it when: someone reports a problem that has no incident yet.

Access: write on incidents. Requires scope `incidents:create` (Register new incidents.).

Errors come back as a tool error whose text is JSON `{"error": "<code>", "message": "..."}`:
- `upstream_rejected`: The Incidents Manager or the inventory refused the request; `field` and the message are theirs.
- `upstream_unavailable`: The service behind the tool did not answer in time, could not be reached, or failed. Retrying later may work.
- `insufficient_scope`: The access token is valid but lacks a scope this tool requires. `required_scopes` and `granted_scopes` say which.
- `invalid_arguments`: The arguments break the tool's input schema or rules; `problems` lists them.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string, min length 1, max length 120 | yes | Short summary of what happened. |
| `description` | string, min length 1, max length 4000 | yes | What happened, with the details a support agent needs. |
| `category` | `lost_parcel` \| `delivery_failure` \| `inventory_discrepancy` \| `carrier_issue` \| `returns_issue` \| `warehouse_incident` \| `system_failure` \| `client_complaint` \| `other` | yes | The kind of incident. |
| `origin` | `customer` \| `branch` \| `internal` | yes | Who reported it: a customer, a branch, or internal staff. |
| `branch` | `central` \| `la_warehouse` \| `la_office` \| `zaragoza_warehouse` \| `zaragoza_office` | yes | The facility it belongs to; `central` when none in particular. |

**Output** (structured content)

```json
{
  "description": "The new incident, as `POST /api/incidents` returns it (`IncidentCreatedResponse`).",
  "properties": {
    "branch": {
      "description": "The facility that manages or reports the incident.\n\n`CENTRAL` is the deliberate catch-all: an incident that does not belong to a\nphysical site still needs a branch, because the field is required for every\norigin.",
      "enum": [
        "central",
        "la_warehouse",
        "la_office",
        "zaragoza_warehouse",
        "zaragoza_office"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "id": {
      "description": "The new incident's id (UUID).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "status": {
      "description": "Lifecycle state of an incident.",
      "enum": [
        "open",
        "in_progress",
        "resolved",
        "discarded"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "id",
    "title",
    "status",
    "branch"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `update_incident_status` — Update incident status

- Required scopes: `incidents:update`
- Access: write on incidents
- Annotations: readOnlyHint=False, destructiveHint=True, idempotentHint=False, openWorldHint=False

Move an incident along its lifecycle through the Incidents Manager's lifecycle endpoint (`PATCH /api/incidents/{incident_id}/status`). Allowed moves: open -> in_progress | discarded; in_progress -> resolved | discarded; resolved: final; discarded: final. Moving to the status it already has is refused too. Returns the updated incident.

Use it when: work on an incident starts, it is solved, or it is dropped. To act on a helpdesk reference ('ticket 482'), call get_incident first to obtain its `id`.

Access: write on incidents. Requires scope `incidents:update` (Move an incident along its lifecycle (status changes).).

Errors come back as a tool error whose text is JSON `{"error": "<code>", "message": "..."}`:
- `incident_not_found`: No incident has that id or helpdesk reference.
- `invalid_status_transition`: The incident lifecycle does not allow that status change; the message says which moves are available.
- `upstream_unavailable`: The service behind the tool did not answer in time, could not be reached, or failed. Retrying later may work.
- `insufficient_scope`: The access token is valid but lacks a scope this tool requires. `required_scopes` and `granted_scopes` say which.
- `invalid_arguments`: The arguments break the tool's input schema or rules; `problems` lists them.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `incident_id` | string, min length 1, max length 64 | yes | The incident's id (UUID), as the Incidents Manager returns it in `id`. |
| `status` | `open` \| `in_progress` \| `resolved` \| `discarded` | yes | The status to move the incident to. |

**Output** (structured content)

### `get_incident` — Get incident

- Required scopes: `incidents:read`
- Access: read on incidents
- Annotations: readOnlyHint=True, destructiveHint=False, idempotentHint=True, openWorldHint=False

Read one incident - its current status and details - from the Incidents Manager (`GET /api/incidents/{incident_id}`, or `GET /api/incidents?reference=` for a helpdesk reference).

Use it when: someone asks about a specific ticket or incident: its status, who reported it, what happened.

Access: read on incidents. Requires scope `incidents:read` (Read incidents: one by id or helpdesk reference, or a search.).

Errors come back as a tool error whose text is JSON `{"error": "<code>", "message": "..."}`:
- `incident_not_found`: No incident has that id or helpdesk reference.
- `upstream_unavailable`: The service behind the tool did not answer in time, could not be reached, or failed. Retrying later may work.
- `insufficient_scope`: The access token is valid but lacks a scope this tool requires. `required_scopes` and `granted_scopes` say which.
- `invalid_arguments`: The arguments break the tool's input schema or rules; `problems` lists them.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `incident_id` | string, min length 1, max length 64 (optional) | no | The incident's id (UUID). Give this or `reference`, not both. |
| `reference` | string, min length 1, max length 32 (optional) | no | The helpdesk reference, e.g. 'TRF-000123', 'TRF-123' or '123' (short forms are normalised). Give this or `incident_id`, not both. |

### `search_incidents` — Search incidents

- Required scopes: `incidents:read`
- Access: read on incidents
- Annotations: readOnlyHint=True, destructiveHint=False, idempotentHint=True, openWorldHint=False

Search incidents in the Incidents Manager (`GET /api/incidents`) by status, category, origin and branch. Filters combine with AND; none lists every incident.

Use it when: someone asks which or how many incidents match a condition, e.g. the open lost-parcel incidents of the Zaragoza warehouse.

Access: read on incidents. Requires scope `incidents:read` (Read incidents: one by id or helpdesk reference, or a search.).

Errors come back as a tool error whose text is JSON `{"error": "<code>", "message": "..."}`:
- `upstream_unavailable`: The service behind the tool did not answer in time, could not be reached, or failed. Retrying later may work.
- `insufficient_scope`: The access token is valid but lacks a scope this tool requires. `required_scopes` and `granted_scopes` say which.
- `invalid_arguments`: The arguments break the tool's input schema or rules; `problems` lists them.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `open` \| `in_progress` \| `resolved` \| `discarded` (optional) | no | Only incidents in this status. |
| `category` | `lost_parcel` \| `delivery_failure` \| `inventory_discrepancy` \| `carrier_issue` \| `returns_issue` \| `warehouse_incident` \| `system_failure` \| `client_complaint` \| `other` (optional) | no | Only incidents of this category. |
| `origin` | `customer` \| `branch` \| `internal` (optional) | no | Only incidents reported by this origin. |
| `branch` | `central` \| `la_warehouse` \| `la_office` \| `zaragoza_warehouse` \| `zaragoza_office` (optional) | no | Only incidents of this branch. |
| `limit` | integer, ≥ 1, ≤ 50 | no | The most incidents to return; `total` still counts every match. Default: `10`. |

### `query_inventory` — Query inventory (read-only)

- Required scopes: `inventory:read`
- Access: read on inventory
- Annotations: readOnlyHint=True, destructiveHint=False, idempotentHint=True, openWorldHint=False

Query inventory data - products and their current stock, one product's stock, or the inbound/outbound movement history - from the inventory (`GET /inventory/products`, `GET /inventory/products/{id}`, `GET /inventory/orders`). READ-ONLY: this server never creates products or records stock movements; any such attempt is refused with `inventory_read_only`.

Use it when: someone asks how much of a product is in stock, in which warehouse, or what came in or went out.

Access: read on inventory. Requires scope `inventory:read` (Read products, stock and movement history. There is no write scope.).

Errors come back as a tool error whose text is JSON `{"error": "<code>", "message": "..."}`:
- `inventory_read_only`: A modification of inventory data was attempted. The inventory is read-only on this server: no scope and no tool can create products or record stock movements.
- `product_not_found`: No product has that id.
- `upstream_auth_failed`: This server could not sign in to the inventory with its service account.
- `upstream_unavailable`: The service behind the tool did not answer in time, could not be reached, or failed. Retrying later may work.
- `insufficient_scope`: The access token is valid but lacks a scope this tool requires. `required_scopes` and `granted_scopes` say which.
- `invalid_arguments`: The arguments break the tool's input schema or rules; `problems` lists them.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `operation` | string, min length 1, max length 64 | yes | The read to perform: `list_products` (products and their stock; filters `sku`, `name`, `warehouse`), `get_product` (one product's stock by `product_id`) or `list_orders` (inbound/outbound movements; filters `warehouse`, `product_id`). Write operations (`create_product`, `record_inbound`, `record_outbound`) are refused with `inventory_read_only`. |
| `sku` | string, min length 1, max length 100 (optional) | no | list_products: exact SKU, e.g. 'SHOE-BLK-42'. |
| `name` | string, min length 1, max length 200 (optional) | no | list_products: words of the product's name, e.g. 'black running shoes'. Every meaningful word must appear in the name or SKU. |
| `warehouse` | `Monterrey` \| `Zaragoza` (optional) | no | list_products / list_orders: only this warehouse. |
| `product_id` | string (uuid) (optional) | no | get_product (required) / list_orders: the product's id. |
| `limit` | integer, ≥ 1, ≤ 50 | no | list_products / list_orders: the most records to return; `total` still counts every match. Default: `10`. |

**Output** (structured content)

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "operation": {
```
